newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Surgutneftegaz in share buy-back scheme.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Surgutneftegaz in share buy-back scheme.

text.p: Russia's AO Surgutneftegaz crude oil producer said on Wednesday it had offered to buy back 500 million ordinary shares at their face value of 1,000 roubles each.
In a company announcement published in the Priob Neft newspaper in the Western Siberian oil town of Surgut, the firm said it would carry out the buy-back scheme from December 9 to January 10, 1997.
AO Surgutneftegaz is the main producing unit of NK Surgutneftegaz, also known as Surgut Holding, which is Russia's third-largest oil company in terms of output and reserves.

Surgut Holding said in October it had raised its stake in producer Surgutneftegaz to 43.5 percent from 38 percent by acquiring a new issue of Surgutneftegaz shares, including 500 million ordinary shares and 34.02 million preferred shares.

The issue, which took some investors by surprise and raised questions over possible share dilution, raised producer Surgutneftegaz' equity to 4.62 billion ordinary shares and 1.37 billion preferred shares.
The Federal Commission for the Securities Market, Russia's main securities watchdog, is investigating that share issue, which was only publicised when Surgut Holding said it had bought the shares.
The commission can recommend to the Finance Ministry to declare the issue void.
